name: Admix
tagline: Multi-model AI chat that compares answers side by side across providers

pricing.notes: Official site lists Admix plans starting at $10/month; the Starter plan is $10/month.

verdictSummary: A local chat UI with side-by-side replies is a weekend project when it calls OpenRouter, but Admix's value depends on access to many hosted models, a current catalog, provider routing, and a maintained account and billing layer. You can reproduce the comparison workflow. You cannot reproduce the model access and service layer for a flat $10 subscription.
coreLoopDIY: Send one prompt to selected models through OpenRouter, stream the replies into a side-by-side grid, and save the thread locally.
requirements: Provider and model IDs to compare
whatYouLose: Admix's bundled access to many providers under one subscription
A maintained model catalog and provider routing
Built-in image, search, and document workflows
Usage limits, billing, and support handled for you
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for one bill and one interface instead of managing several provider accounts, API keys, model IDs, and usage limits. The comparison grid is easy to copy; keeping model access and the account, billing, and storage layer working is the service.

notes: The interface is easy to reproduce; the useful question is whether the API bill and missing provider features still work for you.
prompt:
Build me a local multi-model chat app inspired by Admix. Keep the comparison workflow and do not claim to recreate proprietary models.
Use exactly Node 22, Vite, React, TypeScript, Express, and better-sqlite3.
Start from an empty folder and create a complete working project.
Read OPENROUTER_API_KEY from .env and keep it server-side.
Add a model picker that loads OpenRouter models and lets the user select up to four.
Send one prompt to the selected models and stream each reply into a responsive side-by-side grid.
Show the model name, provider, elapsed time, token usage when available, and clear errors.
Support Markdown, fenced code blocks, copy buttons, and a new thread action.
Save threads, prompts, model IDs, replies, and timestamps in SQLite.
Add search across saved threads and export one thread as Markdown.
Add a usage summary with estimated token cost from OpenRouter usage fields.
Bind to localhost only, with no account, telemetry, analytics, or background jobs.
Explain in the README that prompts and replies leave the machine for OpenRouter, and list permissions.
Add .env.example, clear loading/empty/error states, keyboard-accessible UI, and a responsive layout.
Test model request handling with mocked streaming responses, SQLite persistence, and one browser smoke test.
Add npm scripts for dev, build, test, and start; run the build and tests before finishing.
Leave out auth, billing, mobile apps, image generation, hosted sync, provider-specific tools, and any 100+ model guarantee.
